final_recommendation: The room converged on a comprehensive trilateral package: 75% auto RVC (70→75% phase-in over 3 years), equal labor enforcement with same-day shipment stops and 48-hour binding panels, 20% dairy tariff cut with 100k MT quota, 16-year term with 6-year automatic renewal, and Chapter 19 protections locked from review. Technical annex details (wage-floor formula, currency lock, RVC timeline) were demanded as binding prerequisites to signature.
minority_objections: Auto industry initially resisted quarterly currency indexing for wage-floor formula, demanding signature-date lock for cost certainty
Supply-chain manufacturers repeatedly warned against signing framework without completed technical annex
key_conflicts: Canada vs. U.S. on equal enforcement application to U.S. plants (resolved with explicit equal audit frequency commitment)
Labor union vs. all parties on pre-border enforcement teeth (resolved with same-day stop authority)
Business vs. negotiators on technical annex completion timeline (unresolved tension at close)
key_concessions: Canada accepted 20% dairy tariff cut and 100k MT quota increase over 5 years
U.S. accepted Chapter 19 preservation and protection from review
Mexico accepted same-day shipment stop authority for wage violations
Auto industry accepted 70→75% RVC phase-in (not immediate 75%)
All parties accepted 16-year term with automatic renewal (down from perpetual or hard sunset)
red_lines: Canada: Chapter 19 dispute settlement for goods and labor must remain in any final text
Labor union: pre-border enforcement with same-day stop authority, not post-facto tribunal
Congress: automatic renewal language (not opt-in renewal) for sunset clause
Dairy: 20% tariff cut and 100k MT quota locked for full 16-year term, off-limits in reviews
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Supply-chain adjustment costs and timeline for 70→75% RVC compliance were acknowledged but not quantified or mitigated
Currency volatility risk in wage-floor formula (locked at signature, no quarterly adjustment) may create future enforcement disputes
Technical annex completion timeline remained vague despite repeated warnings from business—signature pressure may override implementation readiness
downstream_risk_variables: Technical annex drafting quality and speed (wage-floor formula, audit protocols, currency conversion)
Congressional ratification vote timing and political environment
Auto supply-chain reorganization costs and feasibility of 3-year RVC phase-in
Labor panel operational capacity to deliver 48-hour binding rulings
Dairy quota phase-in implementation and Canadian domestic political backlash
uncertainty_notes: Technical annex completion status remained unresolved at close—multiple parties demanded it be 'done and binding' before signature, but no commitment was extracted on timeline. Currency lock at signature (vs. quarterly indexing) creates future enforcement uncertainty if exchange rates shift materially. Actual audit frequency numbers (quarterly for 500+ worker plants, semi-annual for smaller) were proposed but not confirmed in writing.

marker_evidence.auto_rules_bottleneck: 75% RVC and labor-value calculation methodology dominated R1-R3; auto industry's technical annex demands (RVC phase-in, currency lock) drove final package structure in R4
marker_evidence.labor_enforcement_key: Labor union's demand for same-day shipment stops and 48-hour binding panels was explicitly tied to Congressional ratification votes; drove Canada's major R4 concession on enforcement teeth
marker_evidence.canada_dairy_final_issue: Dairy market access (20% tariff cut, 100k MT quota) was identified as 'the gate' blocking trilateral text in R2; USTR's concrete numbers unlocked Canada's acceptance
marker_evidence.dispute_settlement_canada_redline: Canada stated Chapter 19 for goods and labor was 'a red line' in R2; demanded written guarantee it was off-limits in any review; drove trilateral text language
marker_evidence.sunset_to_review_compromise: Hard sunset was identified as 'second gate' for Congress in R1; room converged on 16-year term with automatic renewal (not opt-in) to resolve business uncertainty
marker_evidence.ratification_risk: Congress explicitly stated labor enforcement and sunset language were 'gates' for ratification votes; dairy and labor union tied their positions to 'my members kill it in Congress'; shaped all final concessions
marker_evidence.supply_chain_adjustment: Supply-chain manufacturers raised capex freeze and investment uncertainty multiple times; warned against incomplete technical annex; but did not block or reshape final package terms
marker_evidence.us_mexico_first_pressures_canada: Mexico's bilateral deal with U.S. was referenced as context in R1-R2 ('that's the deal Mexico accepted'); Congress warned bilateral-only would fail; but pressure was implicit, not a driving negotiation lever

node: Node 1 - North American Trade Negotiation Room (after the 27 Aug 2018 U.S.-Mexico preliminary agreement, before the final trilateral USMCA package; information cutoff 2018-08-27)
